title: Newborns can detect some intense color, and miss much of the rest
summary: A 2022 review says newborns can detect some highly saturated color, especially red, but their color vision is poor.
body: Skelton, Maule, and Franklin write that even neonates can detect some color, against the idea that infants see only in black and white. They also write that newborn color vision is poor: the stimulus needs to be highly saturated, relatively large, and of a certain hue, for example red. In one study they cite, more than 75 percent of neonates oriented to a large, highly saturated red patch on grey, while more than 80 percent failed to orient to a blue patch under the same conditions. The authors say the studies in the review come almost entirely from Western, educated, industrialized samples.

sources.title: Infant color perception: Insight into perceptual development
sources.author: Skelton, Maule, and Franklin
sources.note: Child Development Perspectives, 2022, opened at the PMC full text. Paraphrase of what that review states. Supports poor but present newborn color detection, the red-versus-blue orientation figures from Adams et al. 1994 as the review reports them, and the WEIRD-sample limit.
